key_insight: Among three phonon-transport models, the first-principles framework best describes thermal transport in AlGaN HEMT thin-film layers and yields the most physically consistent results.
engineering_relevance: More reliable thermal-transport modeling can inform buffer and transition layer design for heat management in AlGaN HEMTs.
method: Compare three models, from a Debye approximation to DFT-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties.
Establish intrinsic transport dominated by Umklapp scattering, then add alloy and boundary scattering.
Fit grain- and film-boundary scattering contributions to measured thin-film thermal conductivity.
evidence_signal: Models were evaluated against Time-Domain Thermoreflectance thermal conductivity measurements, with the first-principles model performing best.
watch_item: Boundary-scattering parameters are fitted to specific samples, so transfer to different film microstructures requires validation.
paper_title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
